<tr id="S5.T3.5.11" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T3.5.11.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.11.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Wavelet-high</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.11.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.11.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.7550</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.11.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.11.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.7229</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.11.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.11.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.7016</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.11.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.11.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.6562</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T3.5.12" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T3.5.12.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.12.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fourier-high</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.12.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.12.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.7629</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.12.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.12.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.7229</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.12.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.12.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.6814</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.5.12.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T3.5.12.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.6373</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.4.2 Head-wise Sparsity ‣ 5.4 Understanding Frequency-Aware Features ‣ 5 Results and Analysis ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table 3</span></a>, a remarkably small fraction of heads accounts for most of the detection performance.
Using only the top 100 heads (less than 10% of all heads in LLaMA-7B) recovers over 95% of the original AUROC across operators and datasets.
This pronounced sparsity indicates that hallucination-related high-frequency attention variation is not a diffuse property shared across all heads.
Instead, a small subset of heads consistently exhibits strong sensitivity to attention instability, suggesting that these heads act as implicit internal indicators of ungrounded generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.4.3 </span>Context v.s. Generated Attention Contribution</h4>

<div id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A critical design choice in our method is incorporating high-frequency attention signals from both source context tokens and previously generated tokens during generation.
We analyze the learned classifier to assess the relative importance of these two sources in practice.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S6.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 6 Broader Related Work ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 6</span></a>, frequency-aware signals derived from context-token attention are consistently more informative for hallucination detection than those from generated-token attention across all spectral operators.
Among them, the Fourier-based method exhibits the largest context–generated importance gap, which aligns with its superior overall performance across tasks and models, suggesting that capturing frequency-aware patterns in context attention contributes to more robust hallucination detection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This asymmetry aligns closely with the core motivation of Lookback-lens <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chuang et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, which emphasizes the role of backward attention to contextual evidence in grounded generation.
Our results extend this view by showing that not only the presence of backward attention, but also its stability and variation, play a critical role in practice. This interpretation is further supported by more ablation results in <a href="#A4.T7" title="Table A7 ‣ D.3 Full Results of Ablation Study ‣ Appendix D Additional Analysis and Results ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table A7</span></a>, where removing only context-based features leads to substantially larger performance degradation than removing only generated-token features.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Broader Related Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we briefly situate our work within the broader literature on hallucination detection in LLMs.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S6.F6.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S6.F6.3.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18145v1/context_vs_generated_l1.svg" id="S6.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/302;" width="405" height="302"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S6.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Average absolute classifier importance assigned to context-attention and generated-attention features over all examined models and datasets.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A substantial line of work detects hallucinations through <span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">external knowledge verification</span>, validating model outputs against curated corpora, knowledge bases, or web search results <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Min et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng et al., 2023b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chern et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. While effective when reliable evidence is available, these approaches are constrained by knowledge coverage, retrieval quality, and inference-time latency, limiting their applicability in on-the-fly detection settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In contrast, <span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">intrinsic detection</span> methods rely solely on model-internal signals and are lightweight enough to operate during decoding. Prior work has explored semantic consistency between input and output, uncertainty and self-consistency across generations, and generation-time statistics such as token probabilities or hidden-state geometry <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qi et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
More recent studies probe attention mechanisms as intrinsic indicators of hallucination <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chuang et al., 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campbell et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which mainly characterize where attention is allocated or how concentrated it is, but largely overlook fine-grained local variation within the token sequence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Using <span id="S6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">frequency-aware</span> tools offers an additional perspective for examining internal model dynamics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kiruluta, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. By modeling internal signals as discrete sequences, frequency-aware representations capture structural patterns that are difficult to characterize using token-level statistics alone. Attention distributions are also typically sparse and highly non-uniform across token positions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nawrot et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, providing a natural basis for frequency-based decomposition, where abrupt allocation correspond to high-frequency components and global distribution patterns align with low-frequency trends.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this perspective, our work introduces a frequency-aware characterization of attention variation as an intrinsic signal for hallucination detection.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This work presents a frequency-aware perspective for analyzing hallucination in LLMs. We show that hallucinated generation is associated with high-frequency variation in attention patterns, revealing a structural property of model behavior that is not captured by attention allocation, transition, or aggregate uncertainty measures. This provides a principled way to distinguish grounded from ungrounded generation based on how attention varies across tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this insight, we introduce a frequency-aware attention modeling framework that extracts high-frequency attention signals using spectral operators. Across multiple models and tasks, our approach improves hallucination detection at both token and span levels, indicating its potential as a generalizable and task-agnostic intrinsic signal for analysis.
Overall, our findings suggest that hallucinations are reflected not only in where attention is placed, but also in how it varies across tokens over time, highlighting frequency-aware analysis as a promising direction for diagnosing and mitigating unreliable LLM generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">

<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents a frequency-aware analysis of internal attention in LLMs for detecting hallucinated generation.
The goal of this work is to advance the understanding and evaluation of LLMs by providing intrinsic signals that can help identify unreliable outputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">There are potential positive societal impacts of this work, including improved reliability and transparency of language model deployments in applications where factual correctness is important.
By relying solely on model-internal signals, the proposed approach avoids dependence on external knowledge sources and may be used as a lightweight evaluation tool.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At the same time, this work does not aim to prevent hallucination or provide guarantees of correctness, and the signals identified should not be used as the sole basis for high-stakes decisions.
As with other analysis and detection methods, responsible deployment requires appropriate safeguards and complementary evaluation mechanisms.
Overall, we believe the ethical and societal implications of this work are aligned with well-established goals in machine learning research, and do not warrant further specific discussion.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>A three-step proof that larger <math id="A1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Goal.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider a <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">single-layer</em> causal self-attention mechanism and measure, at a fixed prediction position <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, how <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rough</em> the attention weights over past positions are as a function of the number of mixture components <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> in the input distribution.
Roughness is quantified by the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> adjacent-difference energy</p>
<table id="A1.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}\;\triangleq\;\sum_{j=1}^{t-2}\big(\alpha_{t,j+1}-\alpha_{t,j}\big)^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.391em">≜</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munderover><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}\;\triangleq\;\sum_{j=1}^{t-2}\big(\alpha_{t,j+1}-\alpha_{t,j}\big)^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\alpha_{t,1:t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t,1:t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the attention row (probability vector) used to predict token <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We prove the claim via three sub-claims:
(i) adjacent tokens switch mixture components more often when <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is larger;
(ii) component switches induce larger adjacent differences in <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">logits</em> <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t,j}</annotation></semantics></math>;
(iii) softmax transfers logit roughness into attention-weight roughness under mild non-degeneracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Setup and assumptions</h3>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mixture of topic labels.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of mixture components. Each position <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> has an associated latent topic label</p>
<table id="A1.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j}\in\{1,\dots,K\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j}\in\{1,\dots,K\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption A.1</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(i.i.d. uniform labels)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(c_{j})_{j\geq 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(c_{j})_{j\geq 1}</annotation></semantics></math> are i.i.d. and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(c_{j}=r)=1/K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(c_{j}=r)=1/K</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\in\{1,\dots,K\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\in\{1,\dots,K\}</annotation></semantics></math>, which means we randomly assign a topic label for the tokens, and each topic has a unique Gaussian distribution. Then, the input token embedding under the view of Gaussian mixture model will follow a GMM:
For each <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A1.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{j}=\mu_{c_{j}}+\varepsilon_{j},\qquad\varepsilon_{j}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle i.i.d.}}{{\sim}}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I_{d})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mover><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mover><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{j}=\mu_{c_{j}}+\varepsilon_{j},\qquad\varepsilon_{j}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle i.i.d.}}{{\sim}}\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I_{d}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{1},\dots,\mu_{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> are fixed means and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\varepsilon_{j})_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\varepsilon_{j})_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent of <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(c_{j})_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(c_{j})_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Then, if we consider a single-layer causal attention at position <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> (the position for the next generated token), and Fix <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Let</p>

<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.5" class="ltx_p">Attention weights from existing token towards next generation token are</p>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Intuitively, Assumption <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption A.4 (Softmax non-degeneracy). ‣ Softmax non-degeneracy (prevents vanishing pair mass). ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a> says that local logit fluctuations happen in parts of the sequence that the softmax actually “looks at”: with nontrivial frequency, the adjacent pair <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(j,j+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(j,j+1)</annotation></semantics></math> receives at least some fixed amount of probability mass, and on those occasions the logit gap is not excessively large. This prevents the situation where logits vary wildly only at positions whose attention weights are almost always zero, in which case attention differences would remain small regardless of logit roughness.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">Taking complements gives <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(c_{j+1}\neq c_{j})=1-\frac{1}{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(c_{j+1}\neq c_{j})=1-\frac{1}{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Sub-claim 2: Adjacent logit difference energy increases with <math id="A1.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma A.6</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Logit adjacent-difference energy)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under Assumptions <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem1" title="Assumption A.1 (i.i.d. uniform labels). ‣ Mixture of topic labels. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>–<a href="#A1.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption A.3 (Separability). ‣ Separability along the score direction. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> and <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption A.2 (Query conditioning). ‣ Mixture of topic labels. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>, for any <math id="A1.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\leq t-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\leq t-2</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text">so that <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t,j+1}-s_{t,j}=A+B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t,j+1}-s_{t,j}=A+B</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text">The cross term vanishes: <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on topic labels <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(c_{j},c_{j+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(c_{j},c_{j+1})</annotation></semantics></math> while <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on Gaussian noises <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\varepsilon_{j},\varepsilon_{j+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\varepsilon_{j},\varepsilon_{j+1})</annotation></semantics></math>, which are independent of labels, and <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}[B\mid c_{j},c_{j+1}]=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[B\mid c_{j},c_{j+1}]=0</annotation></semantics></math>, hence <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[AB]=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[AB]=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the noise term, <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{j+1}-\varepsilon_{j}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2\sigma^{2}I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{j+1}-\varepsilon_{j}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2\sigma^{2}I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math>, so</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\sim\mathcal{N}\big(0,\,2\sigma^{2}\|u\|_{2}^{2}\big)\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathbb{E}[B^{2}]=2\sigma^{2}\|u\|_{2}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\sim\mathcal{N}\big(0,\,2\sigma^{2}\|u\|_{2}^{2}\big)\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathbb{E}[B^{2}]=2\sigma^{2}\|u\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">For the mean-jump term, if <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j+1}=c_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j+1}=c_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{j+1}\neq c_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{j+1}\neq c_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, Assumption <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption A.3 (Separability). ‣ Separability along the score direction. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> gives <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{2}\geq\Delta^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≥</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{2}\geq\Delta^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}[A^{2}]=\mathbb{E}\!\left[A^{2}\mathbf{1}\{c_{j+1}\neq c_{j}\}\right]\geq\Delta^{2}\,\Pr(c_{j+1}\neq c_{j})=\Delta^{2}\Big(1-\frac{1}{K}\Big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[A^{2}]=\mathbb{E}\!\left[A^{2}\mathbf{1}\{c_{j+1}\neq c_{j}\}\right]\geq\Delta^{2}\,\Pr(c_{j+1}\neq c_{j})=\Delta^{2}\Big(1-\frac{1}{K}\Big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">where we used Lemma <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma A.5 (Switch probability). ‣ A.2 Sub-claim 1: Adjacent component switching probability increases with 𝐾 ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.5</span></a>.
Combining yields the stated lower bound.
∎</span></p>

</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Sub-claim 3: Softmax transfers logit roughness to attention roughness</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma A.7</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Pairwise softmax difference identity)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\leq t-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\leq t-2</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=\alpha_{t,j}+\alpha_{t,j+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=\alpha_{t,j}+\alpha_{t,j+1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta s=s_{t,j+1}-s_{t,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta s=s_{t,j+1}-s_{t,j}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then</span></p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma A.8</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Softmax transfer lower bound)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<p id="A1.Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under Assumption <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption A.4 (Softmax non-degeneracy). ‣ Softmax non-degeneracy (prevents vanishing pair mass). ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a> (with <math id="A1.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\leq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\leq 2</annotation></semantics></math>), for any <math id="A1.Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\leq t-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\leq t-2</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<div id="A1.SS4.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">By Lemma <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem7" title="Lemma A.7 (Pairwise softmax difference identity). ‣ A.4 Sub-claim 3: Softmax transfers logit roughness to attention roughness ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.7</span></a>,</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{t,j+1}-\alpha_{t,j})^{2}=m^{2}\tanh^{2}\!\Big(\frac{\Delta s}{2}\Big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>tanh</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{t,j+1}-\alpha_{t,j})^{2}=m^{2}\tanh^{2}\!\Big(\frac{\Delta s}{2}\Big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">On <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{|\Delta s|\leq B\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>s</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0.167em">≤</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{|\Delta s|\leq B\}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\leq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\leq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\Delta s|/2\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\Delta s|/2\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> and use the elementary bound</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Main theorem and concise proof via Sub-claims 1–3</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A.9</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Monotone <math id="A1.Thmtheorem9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-dependent lower bound for attention roughness)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and consider the single-layer causal attention row <math id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\alpha_{t,1:t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t,1:t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> defined in (<a href="#A1.E12" title="Equation 12 ‣ Mixture of topic labels. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).
Under Assumptions <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem1" title="Assumption A.1 (i.i.d. uniform labels). ‣ Mixture of topic labels. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>, <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption A.2 (Query conditioning). ‣ Mixture of topic labels. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>, <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption A.3 (Separability). ‣ Separability along the score direction. ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>, and <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption A.4 (Softmax non-degeneracy). ‣ Softmax non-degeneracy (prevents vanishing pair mass). ‣ A.1 Setup and assumptions ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a>,
there exists a constant <math id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> independent of <math id="A1.Thmtheorem9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">Summing over <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,t-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,t-2</annotation></semantics></math> gives</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A1.SS5.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS5.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text">where the factor <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big(1-\frac{1}{K}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big(1-\frac{1}{K}\big)</annotation></semantics></math> comes from Lemma <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma A.5 (Switch probability). ‣ A.2 Sub-claim 1: Adjacent component switching probability increases with 𝐾 ‣ Appendix A A three-step proof that larger 𝐾 increases (a lower bound on) attention roughness ‣ Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Modelswith Frequency-Aware Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.5</span></a>.
